page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c2d server family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running on an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 64 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks show strong single-core CPU execution, with stress-ng single-core performance placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and cryptography tests fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth is measured at 553.05 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 62.15 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Large-block write bandwidth reaches 39.95 GB/sec. Large-model LLM inference represents a performance tradeoff, with prompt processing for a medium 7B model scoring in the bottom 25% at 18.65 tokens/sec, though text generation for the same model remains average at 10.45 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highmem-8 offers a dense memory configuration relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance. This instance is suited for database operations, memory-intensive web serving, software compilation, and moderate data processing tasks that benefit from a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio without requiring local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
